title: Initial-State-Dictated Dynamical Universality Classes in Quantum Criticality
abstract: The concept of universality class lies at the core of phase transition physics, with each class uniquely characterized by a dedicated set of critical exponents. Here, we introduce the concept of initial-state-dictated dynamical universality classes in nonequilibrium quantum critical dynamics. By studying the imaginary-time relaxation dynamics of the dimerized Heisenberg model, we demonstrate that distinct kinds of initial states can give rise to different dynamical universality classes within the same equilibrium universality class. Specifically, we find that "classical'' paramagnetic (random-spin) and "quantum'' paramagnetic (dimerized and antidimerized) initial states yield drastically different critical initial slip exponents in the bulk. This initial-state dependence also extends to boundary critical dynamics, where different initial states yield different surface critical initial slip exponents even within the same boundary universality class. Remarkably, for the antidimerized initial state, we uncover an anomalous scaling law violating the conventional relation between the bulk and surface critical initial slip exponents. Our results establish an initial-state-controlled dynamical classification of quantum criticality that extends beyond the conventional equilibrium universality paradigm.
summary: This work proposes that quantum critical dynamics are not solely defined by the equilibrium phase, but are also dictated by the initial quantum state. By studying the dimerized Heisenberg model, the authors show that different initial preparations lead to distinct dynamical universality classes. This establishes a new, initial-state-controlled classification scheme for quantum criticality.
main_problem: The paper introduces and investigates the concept of initial-state-dictated dynamical universality classes in non-equilibrium quantum critical dynamics.
main_result: Distinct initial states (e.g., random-spin vs. dimerized) can lead to drastically different dynamical critical exponents, even when the system belongs to the same equilibrium universality class.
method: The study uses imaginary-time relaxation dynamics, analyzed via the projector Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) method and finite-size scaling analysis.
model_or_system: The primary model studied is the dimerized Heisenberg model, which undergoes a continuous Quantum Phase Transition (QPT) belonging to the (2+1)D Heisenberg O(3) universality class.
key_observables: Bulk temporal correlation function ($G_b$) and surface autocorrelation function ($A_s$), characterized by critical initial slip exponents ($	heta$ and $	heta_1$).
important_parameters: The comparison is made across three initial states: random-spin ('classical'), dimerized, and antidimerized ('quantum') paramagnetic states.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the initial state acts as a fundamental determinant of the long-time dynamics, extending the concept of universality beyond equilibrium conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram of the model, and subsequent figures show finite-size scaling collapses for bulk and surface correlation functions for different initial states, highlighting differing exponents.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the framework of dynamical universality, applies it to the dimerized Heisenberg model, and systematically compares the scaling behavior of correlation functions using three distinct initial states, culminating in the discovery of anomalous scaling for one state.
why_interesting: The finding that initial conditions dictate critical dynamics provides a powerful, non-equilibrium generalization of universality, relevant for understanding quench dynamics or preparation protocols in quantum simulation.
